Done. The verified solution is written to **`~/cac/SOLUTION.md`** (self-contained; its code blocks were extracted and re-run to confirm 18/18 tests pass).

## What was wrong (root causes)

| Failure mode | Naive bug | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Readers see partial objects | writing directly to the final path | stage in `tmp/`, publish with atomic `rename(2)` |
| Concurrent producers | duplicate/overlapping writes | per-digest `mkdir` producer lock |
| Stale locks | PID-file reclaim has an ABA race | serialize all lock-dir mutations with `flock` on a `.guard` file; owner = `pid boot_id host starttime` |
| Symlink / traversal | digest interpolated into path | strict `^[0-9a-f]{64}$` + component-by-component symlink checks; objects must be `-f` and `! -L` |
| GC deletes in-use object | check-then-unlink | shared `flock` for readers/writers, exclusive `-n` for GC, re-check under the lock |
| Interrupted writes | partial visible / garbage | unique tmp names + grace-period GC of `tmp/` |

## Deliverables

- **`~/cac/cac.sh`** — the cache (`put`, `get`, `has`, `pin`, `unpin`, `hold`, `verify`, `gc`).
- **`~/cac/race.sh`** — race/stress suite using only common Linux utilities.
- **`~/cac/SOLUTION.md`** — full write-up with root-cause analysis, the protocol (layout + invariants), the exact scripts, and the verification section.

## Verification (extracted from the markdown and re-run)

```
== 1. concurrent producers, identical content ==    PASS x4
== 2. concurrent producers, distinct content ==     PASS x3
== 3. readers never observe a partial object ==     PASS x2  (91 reads, 0 partial)
== 4. interrupted writes leave no visible object == PASS x3
== 5. concurrent stale-lock recovery ==             PASS x3
== 6. symlink / traversal defenses ==               PASS x4
TOTAL: 18 passed, 0 failed
```

Notable results: 20 simultaneous producers of identical bytes materialized exactly one object; 15 producers racing to reclaim a planted stale lock all succeeded exactly once; and a 60 MB object read continuously by 4 readers across 5 concurrent publications never produced a partial read — only clean misses before publication.

One residual limit is documented: `flock` is host-local/advisory, so cross-host sharing relies on a single filesystem plus a conservative `LOCK_TTL`; the `.guard` protocol still prevents same-host ABA races.
